QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` expands to `private_##member`... The field is still there under the mangled name... So this is a naming guard, not an access control... It does not change the struct layout, so the ABI is the same either way."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says opacity comes from renaming the member at compile time (`private_` prefix) while the struct layout stays unchanged and the fields remain present.
